segments.en:
[Untitled — On Saying Psalms]
  תּוֹרָה קכה He spoke with one person about the matter of the recitation of Psalms.

segments.he: מֵעִנְיַן אֲמִירַת תְּהִלִּים דִבֵּר עִם אֶחָד, וְאָמַר לוֹ, שֶׁעִקַּר אֲמִירַת תְּהִלִּים לוֹמַר כָּל מִזְמוֹרֵי תְּהִלִּים עַל עַצְמוֹ, לִמְצֹא אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּתוֹךְ כָּל מִזְמוֹר וּמִזְמוֹר. וְשָׁאַל אוֹתוֹ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה: אֵיךְ. וּפֵרֵשׁ לוֹ רַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה קְצָת, כִּי כָּל הַמִּלְחָמוֹת שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁיַּצִּילֵהוּ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵהֶם, הַכֹּל צְרִיכִין לְפָרֵשׁ עַל מִלְחֶמֶת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע וְחֵילוֹתָיו. וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָּזֶה בִּשְׁאָר הַמִּזְמוֹרִים (וְכַמְבֹאָר מִזֶּה לְעֵיל בְּסִימָן ק"א) וְשָׁאַל אוֹתוֹ, אֵיךְ יְפָרֵשׁ לְעַצְמוֹ בְּהַפְּסוּקִים שֶׁדָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מְשַׁבֵּחַ אֶת עַצְמוֹ כְּגוֹן: "שָׁמְרָה נַפְשִׁי כִּי חָסִיד אֲנִי" וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָּזֶה. הֵשִׁיב לוֹ: גַּם זֶה צְרִיכִין לְפָרֵשׁ עַל עַצְמוֹ, כִּי צְרִיכִין לָדוּן אֶת עַצְמוֹ לְכַף זְכוּת. וְלִמְצֹא בְּעַצְמוֹ אֵיזֶה זְכוּת וּנְקֻדָּה טוֹבָה אֲשֶׁר בִּבְחִינַת הַנְּקֻדָּה טוֹבָה הַזֹּאת הוּא בְּחִינַת חָסִיד וְכַיּוֹצֵא. וְאָמַר לוֹ רַבֵּנוּ זַ"ל: הֲלֹא אֵצֶל יְהוֹשָׁפָט כְּתִיב: "וַיִּגְבַּהּ לִבּוֹ בְּדַרְכֵי ה'" (דִּבְרֵי־הַיָּמִים ב, יז) שֶׁבְּדַרְכֵי ה' וַעֲבוֹדָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הִגְבִּיהַּ לִבּוֹ קְצָת. עוֹד אָמַר לוֹ רַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה: הֲלֹא בַּבֹּקֶר אָנוּ אוֹמְרִים בַּתְּחִלָּה מָה אָנוּ מֶה חַיֵּינוּ וְכוּ', וְאָנוּ מַקְטִינִים עַצְמֵנוּ מְאֹד, וְאַחַר־כָּךְ אָנוּ אוֹמְרִים אֲבָל אֲנַחְנוּ עַמְּךָ בְּנֵי בְרִיתֶךָ וְכוּ', שֶׁאַחַר־כָּךְ אָנוּ מְחַזְּקִים עַצְמֵנוּ וּמְרִימִים אֶת עַצְמֵנוּ וְאָנוּ מְסַפְּרִים אֶת גְּדֻלָּתֵנוּ וּמִתְפָּאֲרִים שֶׁאֲנַחְנוּ עַמּוֹ בְּנֵי בְּרִיתוֹ, זֶרַע אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב וְכוּ'. כִּי כָּךְ צְרִיכִין לְהִתְנַהֵג בַּעֲבוֹדַת ה' כַּנַּ"ל. וְעַיֵּן מִזֶּה בְּסוֹף סֵפֶר הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּסִימָן רפ"ב עַל פָּסוּק: "אֲזַמְּרָה לֵאלֹקַי בְּעוֹדִי":
segments.en:
And said to him: the primary recitation of Psalms is to say all the chapters of Psalms about oneself — to find oneself within every single chapter. And the person asked him, of blessed memory: how? And our Rebbe, of blessed memory, explained to him somewhat. For all the battles that King Dovid, peace be upon him, asked Hashem Yisborach to save him from — all must be explained as referring to the battle of the evil inclination and its troops. And likewise in the other chapters. And he asked him: how should one explain for oneself in the verses where King Dovid, peace be upon him, praises himself — such as: "Guard my soul for I am pious" and the like? He replied: This too must be explained about oneself — for one must judge oneself to the scale of merit. And find in oneself some merit and good point — in which — in the aspect of that good point — one is in the aspect of pious and the like. And our Rebbe, of blessed memory, said to him: Is it not written of Yehoshafat: "and his heart was elevated in the ways of Hashem" [II Chronicles 17:6] — that in the ways of Hashem and His service, may He be blessed — one elevates one's heart somewhat. Further he said: Is it not so that in the morning we first say "What are we — what is our life" etc. — and we greatly diminish ourselves. And afterwards we say "But we are Your people — children of Your covenant" etc. — for afterwards we strengthen ourselves and elevate ourselves — and we recount our greatness — and are glorified — that we are His people — children of His covenant — the seed of Avraham — Yitzchak — and Yaakov etc. For this is how one must conduct oneself in the service of Hashem as above. And see this in the end of the first book — in §282 — on the verse: "I will sing to my G-d while I yet live."

  סוֹף הַסֵּפֶר קִצּוּר לִקּוּטֵי מוֹהֲרַ"ן הַשָּׁלֵם
  — End of the Work —
  Kitzur Likutay Moharan Ha-Shalaim — Part One (Toirahs 1–286) and Part Two (Toirahs 1–92, 106, 107, 125) — fully translated.

  נ נח נחמ נחמן מאומן

  📜 Translator's Summary — Part Two: Toirahs 60–92, 106, 107, 125 [from the Translator]
  Final section of Part Two — key teachings:

  T60 (§1–§4): Wars and bloodshed cause drought. Speaking Torah before unsuitable students also causes drought. Honour of Torah brings rain.

  T61: Time is a product of limited intellect. The greater the intellect — the shorter time becomes. Mashiach's intellect will be so vast that all of world history will be as nothing — and G-d will say: "Today I have given birth to you."

  T62 (§1–§2): The travels of Israel atone for blemished faith. Blemished faith = idolatry = burning wrath. Travel sweetens the wrath and draws compassion.

  T67 (§1–§4): The true Tzadik is the splendour and beauty of the entire world — like the Temple's master. When his name spreads — G-d's Name is magnified. When false famous ones take over — fires come. Rising at midnight and mourning the Temple saves from fires.

  T71 (§1–§4): The primary wisdom is in the Land of Israel. Blemishing G-d's honour drops one to the minds of outside the Land — which are the aspect of conflict. Charity — especially for the Land — rectifies this. The pleasantness of Torah flows from honoured minds.

  T72 (§1–§7): Eternal life comes through seeing oneself with the true Tzadik → mind glimmers → Torah innovations → shame → teshuvah → lowliness is revived. The sign of a true Tzadik: shame falls on you when you hear him. The sign of a false one: arrogance follows.

  T73 (§1–§2): Tehillim is the special remedy for teshuvah — even for one who has no arousal whatsoever. The 49 days of the Omer = 49 gates of teshuvah. Tehillim opens every gate.

  T77 (§1–§3): Every person needs some daily distress — it flows from the fear that runs through the tefillin-mind. Eating in holiness sweetens it and elevates the mouth to human stature.

  T78 (§1–§4): The great Tzadik must sometimes become a simple person — drawing from the hidden pre-Sinai Torah — to give life to all simple people in the world. There is no despair anywhere at all. Even a cry from the lowest depths is never lost.

  T82 (§1–§3): Seeing things go wrong = a sign of arrogance. Teshuvah of Elul = connecting even with the lowest of Israel. Connect yourself — wherever you are — to divinity. All wars and opposing wills are nullified.

  T83 (§1–§2): Rectification of the bris → prayer like arrows → sprouting of Mashiach → Shabbos holiness → body from Gan Eden → raising fallen loves and fears → blazing Torah love that nothing can extinguish.

  T88 §3: There is an angel with subordinates all holding shofars — constantly digging and seeking after lost sparks — blowing t'kiyah — t'ru'ah — t'kiyah. When they find a spark — great joy.

  T91 (§1–§2): All things in the world must be connected to Hashem. The secular speech of true Tzadikim connects even the very distant. Through attachment to true Tzadikim — complete teshuvah, atonement, and the unification of G-d and the Shechinah.

  T92: The Ten Psalms rectification for nocturnal occurrence — listed. One who says them on that same day is certainly rectified. And in their merit — Mashiach will come to gather Israel.

  T125: The primary recitation of Tehillim is to find oneself in every chapter. Apply Dovid's battles to the battle with the evil inclination. Find the good point that makes you the "pious one" in each verse. First humble yourself — then raise yourself — "But we are Your people."

  Completion note: With
